name: Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape
story: On a sandstone hill where the Limpopo and Shashe rivers meet, the Kingdom of Mapungubwe flourished between 900 and 1300 AD — the first indigenous kingdom of Southern Africa. From its hilltop palace, kings traded gold and ivory to the Indian Ocean world, and the famous golden rhino was buried with their royal dead.

story: On a hillside in Kampala, the Kasubi Tombs hold the burial houses of four Buganda kings — the Kabaka. The great thatched building Muzibu Azaala Mpanga, with its 52 ring-beams symbolising the 52 clans, is a masterpiece of organic Ganda architecture and an active spiritual and royal site.
